name: Reply detection and outbound linkage (PCF-08-2)
skipReason: Internal (non-HTTP) service function — it has no route, so the request/response regression runner cannot reach it. It IS executed end-to-end against real Postgres by packages/sdk-conversation/tests/replyDetection.integration.test.ts (10 cases: all four ladder rungs, both recency bounds, the unmatched queue, the late-parent retry and the two schema invariants). The HTTP surface that will exercise it lands with the compose-guardrails-and-routes task.
description: Binds an inbound message to the outbound message it answers, then persists the link on conversation.message (in_reply_to_message_id, reply_link_method, reply_linked_at). Resolution is a four-rung ladder tried strongest first: PROVIDER_REPLY_ID (the provider echoed our own message id — proof), EMAIL_HEADER (In-Reply-To, then References walked newest→oldest — proof), PROVIDER_THREAD_KEY (same carrier conversation or DM thread — strong), and CHANNEL_RECENCY (the most recent outbound on this thread+channel — a heuristic, bounded by CONVERSATION_REPLY_WINDOW_HOURS, default 72h). The rung used is recorded so a consumer can tell a carrier's own echo from a timing guess; the emitted event carries a matching confidence of proof|strong|heuristic. Proves AC1 (inbound replies link to their originating outbound) and AC3 (linkage works across EMAIL via headers, SOCIAL_DM via thread key, and SMS via recency, since SMS carries no threading at all). QA edge cases: resolution only ever considers direction='OUTBOUND' rows, so a mail loop that reflects our own id back on an inbound cannot create a reply-to-a-reply chain; the recency rung requires occurred_at <= the reply's occurred_at, so a backfilled outbound that ARRIVED late can never become the parent of a reply that predates it, and it will not reach past the window, so a reply months later is left for a human rather than attached to a dead campaign; ordering everywhere is by occurred_at (never arrival), matching migration 002. When nothing matches, the message is NOT dropped and NOT failed — it is retained, the trigger forces reply_link_state='UNMATCHED', the provider's claimed parent key is still persisted as evidence, and conversation.reply.unmatched.v1 is emitted (AC4); listUnmatchedInbound() is the triage queue and retryUnmatched() re-runs the ladder so a late-arriving parent links retroactively. Note the emit is best-effort (emitEvent swallows failures), so a successful link does not by itself prove the event was appended — assert the audit ledger, not the return value.

testCases.name: EMAIL: In-Reply-To naming our Message-ID links as proof
EMAIL: falls back to References when In-Reply-To matches nothing
SOCIAL_DM: links by carrier thread key
SMS: no threading signals — recency heuristic, marked as a guess
Recency never reaches past the window, nor forward in time
Unmatched inbound is retained and flagged, never dropped
A late-arriving parent links on retryUnmatched

errorCases.name: Reply detection on a message that was never recorded is refused, not silently skipped
errorCases.message: [sdk-conversation] inbound message <id> not found — record the message before running reply detection; it must never be dropped
errorCases.when: message_id names no row, or names a row whose direction is not INBOUND (an outbound message or an internal note has nothing to be a reply to)

errorCases.name: A resolved parent that cannot be written back is raised rather than reported as linked
errorCases.message: [sdk-conversation] could not link inbound message <id> to <parent_id>
errorCases.when: the ladder resolved a parent but the UPDATE matched no row — the message stopped being INBOUND concurrently, or the resolved parent is the message itself (guarded by message_id <> parent, backing migration 002's conv_message_not_own_reply)

errorCases.name: An unparseable occurred_at is refused rather than sorted to the epoch
errorCases.when: occurred_at is not a Date and not a parseable date string; accepting it would place the reply at 1970 and let the recency rung match the wrong outbound
